newsitem.title: INDIA: India state to invite diamond mining bids by March.
newsitem.headline: India state to invite diamond mining bids by March.

text.p: India's Madhya Pradesh state plans to allow foreign companies to exploit its 11 diamond mines, the state mining minister said on Sunday.
Satya Narayan Sharma told Reuters in the western city of Jaipur that the central state intended to hold a global tender in March for the right to exploit the mines.

"The state cabinet has decided to adopt the route of international competitive bidding for alloting diamond mines, and the ICB (international competitive bidding) would be floated in March this year," he said.
Sharma was in Jaipur, located in the western state of Rajasthan, to attend a conference.
The ICB will cover all 11 mines, and firms will have to bid jointly for all of the mines, he said.
Sharma said ownership of the mines had been transferred to the state-owned Madhya Pradesh Mining Development Corporation, which would enter into a joint venture with the winning bidder.
He did not say how large a stake the Mining Development Corporation would retain in the mines.
The winning company would have to pay royalties on the diamonds and undertake social welfare projects for miners and their families, Sharma said.
The decision to hold a diamond mining tender appeared to be a setback for South Africa's De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd.
De Beers had had an agreement to set up a joint venture with India's Reliance Industries Ltd, said to be estimated at $30 million, to mine diamonds in Madhya Pradesh.
But the state government, under pressure from the Hindu nationalist opposition, later withdrew De Beers's mining lease.
